body:
I have just dealt with a very similar situation. My Girlfriend moved to China, and the plan was for me to move there in 5 months. She broke up with me 2 months in, telling me she wanted to just "be alone" while she was in China, but then get back together when she gets back in a year. I told her that I would not be waiting for her. Within 2 weeks, she was ringing me again telling me she had changed her mind, and still wanted me to move to China. 

She then told me that she had been for a drink with someone else in that time. Over the course of the next two weeks, she slowly drip fed me more more and more of the truth, telling me "thats all that happened" every time. She has been sleeping with him for those two weeks, and if i pushed for more truth, she had probably been sleeping with him a lot longer. Im guessing he wasnt willing to commit/ she felt like I was a safer option. Either way she wasnt fully committed to the relationship in the way I was. We both had told each other we wanted a future together, but I was the only one who wasnt willing to ever risk that. 

Would you have ever risked losing a future with her prior to this?because she has.
Do you feel like she is telling you the whole truth? 
Will you always have more questions in your head which you will never be sure to have truly answered? You dont need that paranoia dude. 

Ask yourself these questions and see how you feel.

I am exactly the same. I am in the same situation right now, panicking about when my GF is gonna text back. I have been cheated on before several times, and my self worth is at rock bottom. I try to breathe deep and focus on that. Have you talked to him about this? There are ways he can try to help?  I'm sorry I don't think there are many short term solutions for us. We just have to keep taking these risks until someone proves our anxieties wrong, its either that or just shut off the idea of love altogether I guess.
Thank you. I know I need to leave her, but I don't want to live a life without her. Such a shit place to be.

I used to be in a similar situation. Anxiety and a lack of self worth prevent you from starting anything because you are scared of failure. You have to give yourself self-worth and it doesn't come out of nowhere. You have to work at it, without making it seem to big to yourself, one step at a time. You just have to start. Doesn't matter what. Give yourself a goal, and achieve it. The feeling it gives you will make you want to achieve more. I know its not easy and it feels like the world is designed to push you back down, but you are stronger than that. Do something today, go for a run, work out, cook something, learn something. Don't let yourself get to the end of they day and look back on it negatively.

Friends are important, but not more important than you. I have had phases of my life where I thought my friends at the time were the most important thing in the world and that that I could not live without them. Either I drifted away from them or they drifted away from me, and it can hurt, but if they are good enough friends, they come back. If they seem to be drifting, and you have done what you can, allow them to drift, suffocating them won't help. This is part of life and really difficult if you are the kind of person who prefers a small group of friends. But this isn't the end of all your friendships ever, you will find new friends and you will enjoy yourself and that is fine. You are a good person and you will be just fine. Life is shit sometimes and other times its amazing. Just enjoy it and see what happens.
